# T5 — Your concept at three zoom levels

Roughly an hour. Write `03-artifacts/concept.md` with exactly three sections. Draft it
**section by section, with pushback** — never in one pass, never as a single generated file
the founder is asked to approve.

## Gating question

None. Everything needed is in `01-company/`.

## The three sections

1. **ONE LINE** — `[who]` gets `[what outcome]` via `[what mechanism]`. No adjectives.
2. **ONE PARAGRAPH** — adds the problem, why now, and what this is unlike (name the current
   alternative by name).
3. **ONE PAGE** — adds how it works, who pays, what they believe that others do not, and the
   three biggest ways this dies.

## How to run it

Take one section at a time. Draft, show, push back, redraft, and only save when the founder
says it is right.

The pushback that matters: **if the one-liner needs an adjective to sound good, the concept
is not sharp enough yet.** Say that out loud when it happens. "Revolutionary", "seamless",
"AI-powered" are the tell.

> **Success moment (per section):** read that back to yourself. If you'd say it out loud to
> a stranger without wincing, it's done.

## verify-M

`03-artifacts/concept.md` exists with three clearly labelled sections, all three non-empty.

## verify-J — rubric (always delivered, never blocks)

Score and say it plainly:

- **A stranger test.** Could someone with no context read each level and understand what the
  business does? Name the specific word or phrase that would stop them.
- **Altitude, not length.** The three levels must differ in *what they contain*, not just in
  how many words they use. A one-page version that is the paragraph with more adjectives has
  failed this rubric — say so directly.
- **Named alternative.** The paragraph names the current alternative. "Nothing" and "doing
  it manually" are legitimate answers; "no one is doing this" is almost never true and is
  worth challenging once.
- **The three deaths are real.** If all three ways this dies are external (market, timing,
  funding), push once for one that is about them or the product.

Deliver the rubric even when everything passes — the founder should see what was checked.

## Success moment

> Your concept at three sizes, saved. That one-liner is the thing you'll say for the next
> year, so it was worth the hour. Task 5 of 9 done.
